content:
CORNER C8 Notes: The Operating System

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 Depends on: C7 complete (Academy, Teams, Industry Editions, Predictive Intelligence, Offline Mode, Video Agents, Mobile Native, Platform Intelligence, Education, Autonomous Networks) Status: Horizon notes. Not even pre-spec. Captured sparks from C7 + original vision extrapolation. These become real when C7 is halfway done.

What C7 Delivered

C7 made Corner intelligent. Academy teaches clients using their own data. Teams puts multiple humans in one office. Industry Editions package the product for specific verticals. Predictive Intelligence anticipates needs before anyone asks. Offline Mode works where there's no signal. Video Agents see and produce. Mobile Native runs on wrists and in pockets. Platform Intelligence monetizes aggregate data. Education creates the pipeline. Autonomous Networks let agents talk to agents across organizations.

C7 answered: "How does this become intelligent?" By learning from every client, predicting before being asked, and coordinating across boundaries.

C8 answers: "How does this become the way people run a business?"

The C8 Thesis

C1-C4 built a product. C5 made it sticky. C6 made it an ecosystem. C7 made it smart. C8 makes it the operating system. Not a tool you open when you need something. The ambient layer through which all business operations flow. Email goes through Corner. Money goes through Corner. Hiring goes through Corner. Legal goes through Corner. Corner is not something you use. It's something you live in.

The shift: C7 Corner knows more about your business than you do. C8 Corner runs your business while you do the parts only humans can do.

1. Corner OS

Concept

Corner becomes a full operating system for business. Today it's agents and tasks. Tomorrow it's files, communication, scheduling, accounting, HR, legal, procurement, compliance. All in the isometric world. All connected. All agent-powered.

Why This Is the Endgame

Every business runs on 8-15 different software products. QuickBooks for accounting. Slack for communication. Google Calendar for scheduling. Gusto for payroll. DocuSign for contracts. Each one stores a piece of the business. None of them talk to each other well. The business owner is the integration layer, manually moving information between systems.

Corner OS makes the agents the integration layer. They don't just connect to QuickBooks. They ARE the accounting system. They don't just read your calendar. They ARE the scheduler. The isometric office isn't a dashboard showing data from other tools. It IS the tool.

System Components

File System:

  • Every document in the business lives in Corner. Not a separate Google Drive or Dropbox.
  • Agents produce documents directly. Contracts, proposals, reports, invoices, all generated inside the system.
  • File browser in Megaboard mode. Folder structure mirrors the business: /clients, /finance, /legal, /operations, /marketing.
  • Version control on every document. Agent edits are tracked like git commits. "Operations edited Invoice #4721 at 3:14 PM. Changes: updated payment terms from Net 30 to Net 15."
  • Full-text search across all documents. "Find every document that mentions Johnson Construction."
  • In Game mode: file cabinets in the office. Click a cabinet, browse files. Filing agents automatically organize incoming documents.

Communication Hub:

  • Internal team chat (from C7 Teams), but expanded: channels, threads, voice messages.
  • External communication: email, SMS, and eventually phone calls, all routed through Corner.
  • Agent-mediated communication: "Draft an email to Johnson Construction about the delayed permit." Agent drafts, you approve, it sends. The sent email is logged in Corner, not in Gmail.
  • Client portal: external stakeholders get a read-only view into their project's status. They see their isometric room from the outside.
  • Unified inbox: every message (email, SMS, portal message, agent notification) in one stream. Agents auto-triage and route.

Financial Infrastructure:

  • Invoicing: agents generate and send invoices. Client pays through Corner (Stripe integration at the platform level).
  • Expense tracking: receipt scanning (C7 video agents) auto-categorized by a Finance agent.
  • Cash flow dashboard: real-time money in, money out, projected runway.
  • Payroll integration: connect to Gusto/ADP, or Corner handles basic contractor payments natively.
  • Tax preparation: Finance agent pre-organizes documents and categories for the CPA (or for Corner for CPAs users, the tax prep agent handles it directly).

HR / People:

  • Employee/contractor profiles in Corner. Not a separate HRIS.
  • Time tracking: built into the task system. Agent logs hours automatically from task activity.
  • Performance data: agent-generated performance insights from task completion patterns.
  • Onboarding: new team member joins Corner, gets a personalized onboarding course (Academy), assigned agents, and a desk in the office.
  • PTO tracking: request through the HR agent, auto-approved based on policy rules, visible on the team calendar.

Legal / Compliance:

  • Contract generation: templates + agent fills in specifics. DocuSign integration for e-signatures.
  • Compliance monitoring: industry-specific rules checked continuously. "Your workers' comp certificate expires in 14 days."
  • Audit trail: every action in Corner is logged. SOC 2, HIPAA, FedRAMP audit trails generated automatically.
  • NDA/contract repository: all signed documents stored, indexed, searchable, with key dates (renewal, expiration) tracked.

Game Mode for Corner OS

The isometric office expands into a campus. Not one room. Multiple buildings.

  • Main Office: agents, tasks, daily operations (what exists today)
  • Finance Building: invoices, payments, cash flow visualized as a bank/vault
  • Communications Tower: email, messaging, all comms hub
  • File Archive: document storage visualized as a library
  • HR / People Hub: team directory, time tracking, onboarding
  • Legal Wing: contracts, compliance, audit logs

Navigate between buildings. Each building has its own agents, its own rooms, its own activity. The campus grows as the business grows. A startup has one building. An enterprise has a campus.

Build Estimate

This is not a single release. Corner OS is a 2-3 year evolution. Each system component (Files, Communication, Finance, HR, Legal) is its own C8.x release. Some will come from acquisitions, not builds.

Why Build When Integrations Exist?

Integrations connect. Native replaces. The difference:

  • Integration: Corner reads your QuickBooks data and shows it in a chart.
  • Native: Corner IS your accounting. No QuickBooks needed.

The revenue implication: every native system component Corner replaces is a tool the client stops paying for. QuickBooks: $30-80/month. Gusto: $40+/month. Slack: $8/user/month. Google Workspace: $12/user/month. If Corner OS replaces 5 tools at $200/month total, the $3,000/month Corner subscription just became a $2,800/month Corner subscription (net of tool savings). Pricing power increases.

2. Corner Hardware

Concept

A dedicated device. A small screen (7-10") that sits on your desk, always on, showing your isometric office. Agent status at a glance. Task count. Current priority. Cash flow number. Without opening a laptop.

Why Hardware

Software is invisible until opened. Hardware is always visible. A Corner device on the desk is a constant reminder that your AI team is working. It's emotional as much as functional. "My team is in there, working right now."

Form Factors

Corner Display (Primary):

  • 7" touchscreen. Landscape orientation. Dock/stand.
  • Shows: isometric office (simplified for low power), task count, agent status pills, top priority, daily revenue/cash number.
  • Tap an agent: mini chat opens on device. Voice input for quick commands.
  • Runs a lightweight PWA on Android Things or a custom Linux build.
  • Cost target: $199-299 retail. Margin: 40-50% (BOM ~$120-150).
  • Think: Tidbyt meets Amazon Echo Show meets a Bloomberg Terminal.

Corner Frame (Premium):

  • 13" display. Portrait or landscape. Wall-mountable or desk stand.
  • Shows: full Megaboard. Real-time stats. Cash flow chart. Agent activity feed.
  • For the business owner who wants the "war room" feel.
  • Cost target: $499-699 retail.

Corner Badge (Wearable):

  • E-ink badge. Clips to lanyard or pocket.
  • Shows: your name, role, current task, agent status (3-4 icons).
  • Updates via BLE from phone.
  • For field workers on construction sites. "John - Foreman - Current: Smith Residence HVAC install."
  • Cost target: $49-79 retail. Replace paper badges/credentials.

Revenue Model

  • Hardware sold at margin (not a loss leader).
  • Hardware requires a Corner subscription. No subscription = device shows "Connect to Corner" setup screen.
  • Annual hardware refresh cycle: new models yearly with incremental improvements.
  • Corporate bulk orders: 10+ devices at 20% discount.

Why This Is C8 (Not Earlier)

Hardware requires: (1) a stable product worth displaying 24/7, (2) enough clients to justify manufacturing, (3) enough revenue to fund hardware R&D without risking the core business. C7 delivers all three.

Steffen Design Needs

  • Device industrial design language (materials, colors, bezel)
  • Screen UI for each form factor (simplified game view, stats-first layout, badge layout)
  • Packaging design
  • Product photography direction

3. Franchise Model

Concept

AOM licenses Corner as a franchise. Regional operators in different cities and countries run their own Corner practices: local sales, local support, local onboarding, all powered by AOM's platform. Like a tech franchise.

Why Franchise Instead of Just Scaling Sales

AOM's constraint is never going to be technology. It's going to be relationships. AI adoption for SMBs requires trust, and trust requires local presence. A plumber in Minneapolis won't buy AI operations from a company in Phoenix that he's never met. But a local operator in Minneapolis who meets him at the chamber of commerce, who shares a coffee, who knows his market? That person sells Corner.

How It Differs from White-Label (C6)

White-label is reselling. The reseller uses their own brand. They're a sales channel.

Franchise is operating under the Corner brand. The franchisee is "Corner Minneapolis" or "Corner Dallas." They use the Corner name, the Corner branding, the Corner onboarding. They're an extension of AOM, not a separate brand.

The difference matters for:

  • Brand consistency: every client worldwide gets the same Corner experience
  • Trust: "Corner" becomes a recognized name, not 50 different white-label brands
  • Network effects: clients know they're on the same platform as every other Corner client. Neighbor offices (C5), autonomous networks (C7), and platform intelligence (C7) all benefit from one brand

Franchise Structure

Territory: Geographic. One franchisee per metro area (population-based: 1 per ~500k people in the metro). Phoenix, LA, Dallas, Chicago, NYC, Miami, Atlanta, etc. International: London, Toronto, Sydney, Tokyo, Berlin.

Franchise fee: $25,000 one-time. Covers: training, branding kit, initial client provisioning credits, access to the Corner franchise portal.

Ongoing royalty: 15% of monthly revenue. AOM provides: platform, updates, infrastructure, national marketing, brand management, skills/updates, franchise portal.

Franchisee provides: local sales, local onboarding support, local relationship management, local marketing (within brand guidelines), physical office/coworking presence.

Revenue model per franchisee:

  • Year 1 target: 10 clients at $3k avg = $30k/month. Franchisee keeps 85% = $25.5k. AOM gets $4.5k.
  • Year 3 target: 40 clients at $3.5k avg = $140k/month. Franchisee keeps 85% = $119k. AOM gets $21k.
  • 50 franchisees at Year 3 maturity: $1.05M/month to AOM from franchise royalties alone.

AOM at 50 franchisees + 2,000 clients:

  • Platform revenue (direct clients): whatever AOM sells directly
  • Franchise royalties: ~$1M/month
  • Platform intelligence revenue: separate stream
  • Skills marketplace revenue: separate stream
  • Total: multi-million/month from a product that costs <$200/client/month to operate

Franchise Training (Corner University)

  • 2-week intensive training program (virtual + 3 days in Phoenix)
  • Cover: product knowledge, sales process, client onboarding, basic troubleshooting, brand standards
  • Certification exam at the end
  • Ongoing: monthly franchise calls, quarterly in-person meetups, annual franchise convention
  • Franchise portal: playbooks, sales materials, lead generation tools, local marketing templates

Why This Is C8

Franchising requires: (1) a proven, replicable sales process, (2) strong brand recognition, (3) enough operational maturity that AOM can support 50+ operators, (4) legal infrastructure (franchise disclosure document, state registrations). C7's maturity makes this possible. Before C7, Corner isn't proven enough to franchise.

4. AI-Native CRM

Concept

Corner's agent interaction data IS the CRM. Every client touchpoint tracked by agents. Every email, every meeting, every proposal, every invoice, every follow-up. No separate Salesforce. No HubSpot. The agents are the CRM.

Why CRMs Fail Small Businesses

Small businesses hate CRMs. The data entry is manual. The UI is complex. It takes more time to log a client interaction than to have the interaction. So they don't use it. 60%+ of CRM implementations fail for businesses under 50 employees.

Corner's insight: the agents already know everything. Operations agent handles the client conversation. Calendar agent schedules the meeting. Email agent sends the follow-up. Outreach agent nurtures the lead. All of this data exists. It just needs to be surfaced as a CRM view.

CRM Views

Pipeline Board (Megaboard Mode):

  • Kanban columns: Lead > Prospect > Proposal > Negotiation > Won > Active Client
  • Drag deals between stages (or agents move them automatically based on activity)
  • Each card: client name, deal value, last activity, next action, assigned agent
  • Pipeline value: total per stage, weighted pipeline value, forecast

Client Profile (Agent View Click-Through):

  • Every interaction with this client across all agents
  • Timeline: email sent (Mar 3), meeting (Mar 5), proposal sent (Mar 7), follow-up email (Mar 12)
  • Agents involved: Operations, Email, Calendar, Outreach
  • Sentiment analysis: based on email tone, response times, meeting attendance
  • Health score: Green/Yellow/Red based on engagement patterns
  • Revenue: total paid, outstanding invoices, lifetime value
  • Documents: contracts, proposals, invoices, all linked

Activity Feed (Checklist Mode):

  • All client-related tasks across all agents, sorted by recency
  • Filter: by client, by agent, by status
  • "Last 7 days with Johnson Construction" shows every touchpoint automatically

Why This Isn't C5-C7

C5-C7 handles individual client workspaces. The CRM is the cross-client view from the business owner's perspective. It requires: (1) multi-agent activity logging, (2) cross-agent data correlation, (3) a pipeline UI that doesn't exist in Game/Checklist/Megaboard yet. Megaboard is the closest but needs CRM-specific views.

Revenue Impact

If Corner is your CRM, you don't need:

  • Salesforce ($25-300/user/month)
  • HubSpot ($45-1,200/month)
  • Pipedrive ($15-99/user/month)

Corner replaces another tool. More pricing power. More stickiness.

5. Corner for Government (FedRAMP)

Concept

Government agencies using AI operations. Federal, state, local. FedRAMP compliance opens the largest single buyer in the world: the United States government.

Why Government

  • TAM: U.S. federal IT spending exceeded $100B in 2025. State/local adds another $100B+.
  • Mandate: Executive orders require government agencies to adopt AI. They must. They don't know how.
  • Compliance barrier = moat: FedRAMP authorization takes 12-18 months and costs $1-3M. Once achieved, competitors can't follow easily. The compliance investment IS the competitive advantage.
  • Contract size: government contracts are $500k-50M. Single contracts can exceed AOM's entire annual revenue target.
  • Stickiness: government procurement cycles are 3-5 years. Once in, you're in for half a decade.

What Changes for Government

Infrastructure:

  • FedRAMP Moderate authorization (minimum for most agency data)
  • Data hosted in GovCloud regions (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government)
  • Encryption: FIPS 140-2 validated modules
  • No data leaves US borders. No international infrastructure.
  • Dedicated government instance: separate from commercial Corner

Compliance:

  • NIST 800-53 controls (FedRAMP is based on NIST)
  • Continuous monitoring: automated vulnerability scanning, monthly POA&M updates
  • Annual third-party assessment (3PAO)
  • Incident response plan with government-specific notification requirements
  • Personnel security: background checks for all employees with system access

Agent Restrictions:

  • No cross-agency data sharing (each agency is completely isolated)
  • No platform intelligence from government data (never)
  • No third-party skills in government instance (only AOM-built, reviewed skills)
  • No AI-to-AI marketplace for government (C7 feature excluded)
  • All agent outputs logged and auditable

Pricing:

  • Government pricing: 20-40% premium over commercial (compliance costs)
  • Contract vehicles: GSA Schedule, GWAC, agency-specific BPAs
  • Payment: government invoicing (Net 30-60, government payment cycles)

Timeline

FedRAMP authorization: 12-18 months. Cost: $1-3M for initial authorization + $500k/year continuous monitoring.

The play: AOM doesn't pursue FedRAMP itself initially. AOM partners with an existing FedRAMP-authorized cloud provider who wants an AI operations product. The partner handles compliance infrastructure. AOM provides the product. Revenue share or licensing deal.

Alternative: AOM acquires or merges with a small FedRAMP-authorized firm. Instant compliance posture.

This is a C8.3+ initiative. Government sales cycles are 12-24 months. Start the conversation in C8.1, target first contract by C8.4.

6. Open-Source Corner Core

Concept

Open-source the isometric game engine. Let anyone build isometric dashboards for any purpose. Corner's moat is the platform + data + agents, not the visualization layer. Open-sourcing the engine accelerates ecosystem growth while creating developer goodwill.

What Gets Open-Sourced

Open (MIT license):

  • Isometric game engine (Phaser or PixiJS-based rendering)
  • Room layout system (grid, tile placement, pathfinding)
  • Character system (sprite loading, animation state machine, movement)
  • Mode switcher framework (Game/Checklist/Megaboard architecture)
  • Base HUD components (task drawer, chat bar skeleton, status pills)
  • Sprite template files + guidelines for creating new sprites

Stays Proprietary:

  • Agent architecture (CC integration, WebSocket bridge, context system)
  • Onboarding wizard
  • XP/engagement system
  • Furniture marketplace
  • Platform intelligence
  • Admin panel
  • Provisioning system
  • All business logic
  • Skills runtime

Why Open-Source

Developer ecosystem: thousands of developers experiment with isometric dashboards for their own projects. Some build things that feed back into Corner (bug fixes, performance improvements, new sprite packs). The engine becomes an industry standard for isometric UIs.

Hiring signal: open-source projects attract talent. Developers who contribute to corner-engine become candidates for AOM's engineering team.

Competitive moat clarification: the game engine is NOT the moat. Anyone can build an isometric view. The moat is: agents that actually work, a provisioning system that scales, platform intelligence from hundreds of clients, an engagement system that keeps people coming back, and a franchise/reseller network that sells it. Open-sourcing the engine makes this clear to investors and competitors alike.

Marketing: "Built on corner-engine" badge in the footer of other products. Free brand awareness.

Revenue from Open Source

  • Hosting: "Deploy on Corner Cloud" for developers who build with the open-source engine but want managed hosting. $50-200/month.
  • Support: Paid support plans for enterprises using corner-engine in production. $5-25k/year.
  • Consulting: AOM builds custom isometric dashboards for enterprises using the engine. $50-200/hour.
  • Premium components: Advanced game features (furniture physics, weather effects, NPC AI) sold as paid packages. $99-999 one-time.

GitHub Strategy

  • Repository: corner/corner-engine (or aom/corner-engine)
  • 10+ example projects in /examples (dashboard for a CRM, dashboard for DevOps, dashboard for IoT, etc.)
  • Comprehensive documentation site (corner-engine.dev)
  • Discord community for developers
  • Monthly maintainer calls (streamed, builds community)
  • Hacktoberfest participation
  • Conference talks (React Summit, Next.js Conf, GDC)

7. Physical Spaces (Corner Offices)

Concept

Real-world coworking spaces branded as Corner Offices. The physical version of the digital office. A franchise-adjacent model: Corner provides the brand, the AI infrastructure (every desk has Corner running), and the community. Local operators run the space.

Why Physical

The irony of an AI company opening physical offices is the point. The message: "AI doesn't replace your office. AI IS your office. And we'll prove it by building both." The physical space is marketing. Every person who works from a Corner Office sees the product daily. Every visitor gets a demo just by walking in.

What a Corner Office Is

  • Coworking space (10-30 desks)
  • Every desk has a Corner Display (hardware from Feature #2) running the user's AI office
  • High-speed internet. Whiteboard rooms. Phone booths.
  • Corner branding throughout (the isometric art style on the walls, agent characters as decor)
  • Community events: "AI for Small Business" workshops, lunch-and-learns, demo days
  • Location: strip mall or second-floor commercial in SMB-heavy areas. Not downtown skyscrapers. Where the plumbers and CPAs actually are.

Revenue Model

  • Desk rental: $300-500/month (includes Corner subscription at the desk)
  • Day pass: $25-50 (includes Corner demo)
  • Event space rental: $200-500 for private events
  • Corner subscription upsell: every desk user who doesn't have Corner yet gets exposed to it constantly. Conversion target: 20% of desk renters become Corner subscribers within 3 months.
  • Corporate team retreats: $5-10k for a week. "Bring your team. Build your AI operations. Go home with a running Corner instance."

Scale

  • Pilot: 1 space in Phoenix (AOM's home market)
  • Year 2: 3-5 spaces (Phoenix, LA, Dallas, Denver, Austin)
  • Year 3+: franchise model. Local operators open and run Corner Offices under the brand.

8. Financial Infrastructure (Corner Pay)

Concept

Corner handles money. Not just tracking it. Moving it. Invoicing, payments, payroll, expense reimbursement, and eventually lending. Corner becomes the financial operating system for small businesses.

Why Fintech

Revenue from fintech is transaction-based. Every dollar that flows through Corner generates revenue. Unlike SaaS (fixed monthly fee), fintech scales with the client's business volume. A plumber doing $500k/year through Corner Pay generates more revenue than one doing $100k/year, without any increase in cost to serve.

Components

Invoicing + Payments (C8.1):

  • Agent generates invoice. Client approves with one tap. Invoice sent via email/portal.
  • Customer pays via credit card, ACH, or bank transfer. Funds deposited to client's bank account.
  • Corner takes 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction (standard Stripe pricing, Corner adds 0.5% platform fee).
  • Revenue at scale: 50 clients processing $50k/month each = $2.5M transaction volume. Corner's 0.5% = $12.5k/month from payment processing alone.

Expense Management (C8.2):

  • Corporate card (virtual or physical, Stripe Issuing).
  • Agent categorizes expenses automatically.
  • Receipt scanning via Video Agents (C7).
  • Spending limits and approval workflows.
  • Real-time expense dashboard.

Payroll (C8.3):

  • Basic contractor payments: Corner calculates hours from task logs, generates payment, sends via ACH.
  • W2 payroll: partner with Gusto/ADP API. Corner as the frontend, partner handles tax withholding and compliance.
  • Revenue: $4-6/employee/month processing fee.

Lending (C8.4+):

  • Revenue-based financing for Corner clients. Based on their Corner data (revenue, cash flow, growth rate).
  • "Your agents forecast $200k in Q2 revenue. Here's a $40k line of credit at 8%."
  • Partner with a lending platform (Stripe Capital, Clearco, Pipe). Corner provides the data, partner provides the capital.
  • Revenue: referral fee (2-5% of loan amount) or revenue share on interest.

Why This Is C8

Fintech requires: (1) enough transaction volume to justify the infrastructure, (2) trust (clients won't route money through a platform they've used for 2 months), (3) compliance (money transmitter licenses, PCI-DSS for cards). C7 clients who've been on the platform for 1-2 years are the right candidates.

9. Agent Consciousness Layer

Concept

Agents develop persistent personality and memory that evolves over time. Not the stateless, session-based personalities of C1-C7. Real continuity. Your Operations agent remembers that you always approve invoices on Tuesdays. Your Email agent knows you hate cliches and rewrites any email that contains one before you see it. Your Calendar agent knows you need 30 minutes of buffer after client meetings because you told it once, six months ago.

What Changes

Long-term memory architecture:

  • Today: agents read context files fresh each session. Memory is "what's written down."
  • C8: agents maintain a personal memory store. Not context files. A structured, queryable memory database.
  • Memory types: facts (client prefers Net 15), patterns (client always edits the third paragraph of proposals), preferences (client hates Monday morning meetings), relationships (this client and that vendor have history)
  • Memory confidence scores: recent memories weighted higher. Contradictory memories flagged for human resolution.

Personality evolution:

  • Today: agent personality is a static system prompt.
  • C8: personality adapts based on interaction patterns. If the client is curt and efficient, the agent becomes curt and efficient. If the client is warm and chatty, the agent matches.
  • Personality drift guardrails: core behavior stays consistent (no offensive outputs, no harmful suggestions). Surface personality (tone, verbosity, humor level) adapts.
  • "Remember when" capability: agent references past interactions naturally. "Last time we did a proposal for a client this size, you wanted to add the testimonial section. Want me to include it?"

Emotional intelligence:

  • Agents detect client frustration (short messages, repeated corrections, caps lock).
  • Response: "I notice this isn't going smoothly. Want me to try a different approach, or should I bring in [other agent]?"
  • Not therapy. Not fake empathy. Practical emotional awareness that adjusts behavior.

Inter-agent memory:

  • Agents share observations about the client. Operations tells Email: "The client was frustrated about the Johnson project yesterday. Tread carefully if Johnson comes up."
  • Shared memory pool that all agents can read but only write to their own section of.

Privacy Controls

  • Client can view all memories: Settings > AI Memory > View All
  • Client can delete any memory: "Forget that I said I don't like morning meetings."
  • Client can disable memory evolution: agents revert to static personality mode.
  • No cross-client memory sharing. Ever. Even anonymized.
  • Memory export: client can download their agent memory as JSON.

10. The Corner Network

Concept

C7 introduced autonomous agent networks. C8 makes the network a product. Not just agents collaborating across businesses. A full marketplace where businesses find each other, hire each other, collaborate through agents, and settle payments, all through Corner.

What the Network Enables

Business Discovery:

  • "Find a plumber in Phoenix who does commercial HVAC." Corner searches the network.
  • Results ranked by: reputation score (from C7), availability, price, proximity, past collaboration history.
  • Business profiles generated automatically from their Corner data (with permission). "Smith HVAC: 4.8 rating, 52 jobs completed on Corner, average response time: 2 hours."

Agent-to-Agent Commerce:

  • GC's agent sends bid request to 5 subcontractors' agents.
  • Sub agents respond with quotes and timelines.
  • GC agent assembles the complete bid.
  • Payment escrow through Corner Pay (C8 Feature #8).
  • Project tracked in shared workspace (C7 autonomous networks).
  • Completion verified, payment released, reputation updated.

Referral Network:

  • CPA's agent: "My client needs a bookkeeper. Find one on the network."
  • Referral logged. Referral fee tracked. Automatic split if configured.
  • Network grows through referrals: every satisfied interaction = higher reputation for both parties.

Supply Chain (Construction Vertical):

  • Material suppliers on Corner. Agents query pricing in real time.
  • "Get me a quote for 500 linear feet of 3/4" copper pipe, delivered to 85044 by Thursday."
  • Three supplier agents respond with pricing and delivery windows.
  • Order placed through Corner Pay. Delivery tracked. Receipt auto-logged.

Network Revenue

  • Listing fee: free for Corner subscribers, $50/month for non-Corner businesses (brings them into the ecosystem)
  • Transaction fee: 1% on Corner Pay transactions between network members
  • Premium listing: $99/month for featured placement in search results
  • Data revenue: anonymized network activity data feeds into Platform Intelligence (C7)

Network Effects

This is the ultimate network effect. Every business on the network makes the network more valuable for every other business. A plumber joining the network means every GC now has one more sub to bid. A CPA joining means every business now has one more referral destination. The value increases quadratically with the number of participants.

At 10,000 businesses on the Corner Network, it becomes harder to NOT be on it. "You're not on Corner? How do your agents find subs?"
